A new optional classic theme, plus dark/light mode switching that no longer leaves stale state behind.

## ✨ Added

- **New `JD_THEME=JDDEFAULT` option: JDownloader's own classic Synthetica look**, alongside the existing `Dark` and `Light` Carbon/FlatLaf themes. Default stays `Dark`; this is purely opt-in for users who prefer the stock UI. Contributed by [@milfer322](https://github.com/milfer322) in [#19](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/jdownloader/pull/19).
- Each theme mode now keeps fully independent LAF state — switching between Dark, Light, and JDDEFAULT (including on an already-initialized container) no longer risks leftover state from a previous mode.
- Three targeted guards against known Synthetica crashes: a disabled-icon `ClassNotFoundException`, a progress-bar gradient `NullPointerException`, and a scrollbar-painter crash from LAF options not being ready yet. None of these can surface under JDDEFAULT anymore.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Switching from JDDEFAULT back to Dark or Light wasted about 3 minutes on a doomed bootstrap.** The launcher didn't know a previous JDDEFAULT run parks `flatlaf.jar` under a different filename, so every switch back ran a full headless JD relaunch and a 36-step polling loop trying to fetch a file that was sitting right there the whole time. It now restores the parked jar first, so the switch takes seconds instead of minutes.

## Verification

Boot-tested on real containers (not just log review), each mode's Look-and-Feel confirmed against the runtime ground truth file: fresh Dark, Dark → Light, Light → JDDEFAULT, JDDEFAULT → Dark (switch-back), and a fully fresh JDDEFAULT install. Every mode reached the READY banner as the log's last block, with no Metal fallback and no self-heal intervention needed.
